# 100.00 USD paid out as one transaction clearing the payable with two splits.
#
# The bill side of `money_arriving_as_two_receivable_splits.txt`, and the same
# fact about the vendor: the money left once, so it is one payment written as
# one `payment:` block. A bill posts the other way round, so its settling
# splits are positive where an invoice's are negative — which is what
# `payment_amount_text` has to sum over.
#
# `print-bill` had no grouping of its own before this, so a bill settled by one
# two-split transaction printed two `payment:` blocks — the bill having been
# paid twice, which is a different fact about the vendor — while the same
# book's `export` wrote one.
#
# All three sides are USD, so the entry is USD and no rate is involved.
#
# What this fixture produces: a USD transaction with three splits, two of them
# on the payable and neither in a lot until a payment block claims them.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
